evidence: FB2-SAF-SEC-000005's safety_allocation.safety_goal_ref is 'FB2-SAF-SCO-000001'. No artifact with that id exists in either profile. The corpus's safety-case skeleton is FB2-SAF-SCS-000001. The reference is also self-contradictory with the field's own prose: the mitigation text says 'traced to the project's safety-case skeleton' and the standard_id is ISO_26262_2018 rather than an argument record, so the value appears to be a mistyped safety-case id. The reference sits inside a required field of the requirement schema (safety_allocation.safety_goal_ref), which is a free string and so accepted a typo the link registry would have caught had the value been expressed as a link.
impact: The requirement whose reference is broken is the one covering entropy and third-party component governance, and it is the requirement this pass had the least verification leverage over: its own rationale records that the observed source derives the initial sequence number from a single 32-bit state seeded with a build-time literal, and that an ungoverned component set is an open item. A requirement in that position whose safety allocation points at nothing cannot be traced into a safety argument by a reader who follows the field. The defect is invisible to the link validator because the value is not a link: it is a string inside a required payload field, and no check resolves strings in payload fields.
root_cause: The value was typed rather than linked. safety_goal_ref is a schema-required string in a record whose siblings use it correctly, and the mistyped id is one character away from the correct one, which is characteristic of hand entry rather than of a stale reference after a rename. The corpus has no check that resolves the string against the artifact index.
resolution:
RESOLVED, and the vocabulary member is corrected from 'accepted' to 'resolved'. No change to the substance: the record was already correct and named its fix. Re-verified on 2026-09-30T00:00:00Z: FB2-SAF-SEC-000005.safety_allocation.safety_goal_ref resolves to a live record. The second instance of the same mistyped id, in FB2-SAF-TAR-000001 threat THR-008, was corrected in the same pass, which is what confirmed the root cause as hand entry rather than a stale reference after a rename - a mistyped value appearing in two records is not what a rename leaves behind. docs/artifacts/tools/check_references.py now resolves every id-shaped string in every corpus and scenario record against the artifact index and the four registries, so this class of defect is detectable rather than invisible, and the TARA's own limitation text records that the security requirements are forward-engineered for a hypothetical project.

Nothing about the record's engineering content changed: no acceptance criterion, ASIL value, verification approach, threat description, likelihood, impact or residual risk was altered by the correction. human_approval_status remains pending, production_authorized remains false and product_verification_credit remains false. No human approved this revision, no tool is claimed to be qualified, and no certification, ISO 26262 conformity or ASPICE capability level is claimed or implied.
